title: Reliable AI Agent Workflows
goal: explain how to move AI agents from demos to dependable internal workflows

story.thesis: The next leap in agent quality comes from workflow closure, not larger prompts.
arc: AI agents can already produce impressive task-level results.
Production use fails when context, permissions, verification, and recovery are missing.
A closed workflow architecture makes agents observable, auditable, and repairable.

slides.title: Reliable AI Agent Workflows
slides.subtitle: From impressive task runs to dependable internal systems
slides.presenterNotes: Open by separating model capability from operational reliability.

slides.title: What we need to close
slides.subtitle: A practical map for making agent runs trustworthy.

slides.title: The fragile part is the workflow around the model
slides.kicker: Most agent failures happen before or after the model response: context collection, tool execution, review, export, and recovery.

slides.headline: Reliability comes from closing the loop around each generated artifact.
slides.evidence: Teams that treat verification as part of generation ship fewer manual cleanup steps.

slides.title: Separate model judgment from system guarantees
slides.subtitle: The architecture is strongest when each layer has one job.

columns.heading: LLM responsibilities
columns.body: The model owns intent interpretation, story, content tradeoffs, and repair reasoning.

columns.heading: System responsibilities
columns.body: The runtime owns schema validation, rendering, screenshots, exports, and audit trails.

slides.title: Free-form generation vs. closed workflow
slides.subtitle: The same model behaves differently when the system gives it rails.

left.label: Free-form HTML
left.headline: Fast, but inconsistent
points: Layout decisions are repeated on every slide

slides.title: A staged path to production
slides.subtitle: Each phase adds one new layer of confidence.

events.label: Phase 0
events.title: Schema and renderer
events.description: Lock the deck contract and produce stable HTML.

events.label: Phase 1
events.title: Visual checks
events.description: Screenshot every slide and report layout failures.

events.label: Phase 2
events.title: Exports
events.description: Generate PDF and PNG artifacts from the same source.

events.label: Phase 3
events.title: Repair loop
events.description: Feed verification reports back into spec repair.

slides.title: Quality signals worth tracking
slides.subtitle: These checks turn vague polish into observable release criteria.

metrics.label: Schema errors
metrics.detail: Deck specs must validate before rendering.

metrics.label: Export parity
metrics.detail: PDF and PNG match browser layout.

slides.title: The renderer consumes a contract, not a prompt
slides.subtitle: A small spec is easier to validate, repair, and diff.
slides.caption: The LLM edits structured content while layouts and themes stay reusable.

slides.title: Make verification part of generation
slides.subtitle: The path to dependable agent output is a closed loop: plan, spec, render, verify, repair, export.
slides.takeaway: Treat every artifact as something the system can inspect before a human has to trust it.
